title: Media Release: New Fuel and LPG Prices for May 2026
text:
MEDIA RELEASE
NEW FUEL AND LPG PRICES FOR MAY 2026
THURSDAY, 30 APRIL 2026
The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission (FCCC) wishes to inform all Fijians of the revised
fuel prices effective from Friday, 1 May 2026.
FCCC notes recent public commentary regarding the methodology applied in its April 2026 fuel price
assessment. The Commission confirms that its pricing framework remains consistent and is applied
using verifiable international data. During periods of heightened volatility, adjustments to the
assessment window may be applied to better reflect prevailing market conditions and to moderate
sudden price shocks to consumers. These are within our regulatory tools to do so.
Measures to Cushion Impact
Global fuel markets have been extremely volatile from March to April 2026. Rather than passing the
full cost increase on immediately, FCCC used a gradual approach to spread the impact over time.
Without this approach, diesel alone could have exceeded $4.50 per litre in May. We chose to absorb
that shock gradually rather than hit households and businesses all at once.
For the assessment period, the following factors attributed to the increase in fuel products.
(i) The price of motor spirit and premix is based on the international refined price and
international freight benchmarks, which reflected the increase in the international refined
fuel price and international freight rate for motor spirit by 33.98% and 48.72%, respectively
while the USD currency weakened by 0.11%.
(ii) The price of kerosene and diesel will also increase due to the increase in the international
refined fuel price of kerosene and diesel by 60.38% and 69.60% respectively. In addition,
the international freight rate increased by 48.72% while USD currency strengthened by
0.70% and 0.43% for kerosene and diesel when compared to the last review.
Under the new pricing, diesel will increase by 93 cents per litre, (32.18%), kerosene by 59 cents per
litre (24.58%), motor spirit by 20 cents per litre (6.83%), and premix by 22 cents per litre (7.97%) in
areas within 3 kilometres of a public road on Viti Levu. Similar increases apply across all other regions
in accordance with the approved price schedules.

Ensuring Fuel Supply Security
At this time, Fiji’s priority remains for continuous availability and sustainability of fuel supply across the
country. In the current global environment, securing fuel shipments may require procurement at
relatively higher costs. The FCCC acknowledges that while prices may increase, ensuring that
suppliers are able to access, and secure supply is critical to prevent shortages and maintaining
economic stability.

World Market Reasons on Crude Oil Prices
According to OPEC, the crude prices rose sharply in March 2026, which were supported by disruptions
to crude oil and petroleum product flows and deteriorated regional shipping operations in the Middle
East and the Gulf Region. These developments tightened physical markets and led to increase in the
demand for prompt crude replacement from other regions such as the Atlantic Basin, North Sea,
Caspian, Mediterranean and Aisa-Pacific.
The sharp rise in crude prices was accompanied by elevated volatility and heavy trading throughout
the month, reflecting heightened uncertainty about near-term supply availability and the rising risk
premium associated with disruptions to Middle East trade flows. At the same time, the oil there were
growing concerns about tightening prompt supply conditions.
Concerns over prolonged geopolitical risks dominated market sentiment, largely overshadowing other
developments, including reports of larger-than-expected build up in the US commercial crude stocks
over the month, coordinated crude oil releases from the Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR) and
indications that certain sanctioned oil shipments were temporarily allowed to proceed. These global
factors contributed to the changes in local refined fuel prices in Fiji effective 1 May 2026.
In addition, FCCC has also concluded the assessment of Butane Contract Price (CP), freight rates
and exchange rates which is reflected in the domestic price of Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices.
The new prices come into effect from Friday, 1 May 2026 and are as follows:

LPG Price Change Factors
The major reasons for the increase noted in the prices for cylinder products, Bulk and Autogas, the
Butane CP remained at USD540/tonne while the international freight rate increased by USD0.16/tonne
on average when compared to the last review in USD. The exchange rate strengthened by 0.62% on

average when compared to the last review. The unfavourable movement in exchange rate outweighed
unchanged movement in the contract prices for Butane and the increase in international freight rate in
May 2026 leading to an increase in LPG Cylinder Prices, Bulk and Autogas in the Fijian market for
May 2026.
World Market Reasons
The LPG Contract Price (CP), commonly called the “Saudi CP” is the international price benchmark
set at the beginning of each month by Saudi Arabia’s state - owned oil company Saudi Aramco. Fiji is
a price taker of the refined fuel products and LPG products, as our country’s domestic demand needs
for LPG is insignificant when compared to the world demand. Saudi Aramco has set its March 2026
term contract price for propane at USD 545/MT and butane at USD 540/MT, same as of February
2026 CPs. Saudi Aramco has suspended shipments of LPG from its Juaymah terminal in Ras Tanura
"for the next few weeks" after part of its export infrastructure was damaged.
Enforcement and Compliance
As part of the FCCC’s enforcement and compliance of fuel and LPG prices, our Enforcement Team
will conduct inspections at wholesale / retail outlets and service stations to ensure authorised prices
of Petroleum and LPG products comply with the allowable maximum prices. The following FCCC
officers will conduct inspections in various divisions:
The Central team can be reached via mobile phone number 8921991 or 9988917 for Nausori
residents. The Western Team can be reached via mobile phone number 8911623 or 9982437 for
Sigatoka residents. The Northern Team can be reached via mobile phone number 8911624.
The prices issued by FCCC are maximum wholesale and retail prices, and the wholesalers and
retailers can sell the Refined Fuel and LPG products on the maximum wholesale and retail prices or
below the authorised prices. The FCCC inspectors will continue to conduct checks during the coming
weeks to ensure ongoing compliance.
